purpose: One confirmatory arm with every Phase A and Phase B repair in place, plus the three previously disabled loss/sampling paths enabled.
weight_rationale: Both new terms are set to 1.0 to match every other term in the existing objective (supervised_u, supervised_P, equilibrium, constitutive are all 1.0). No screening grid is run and no selection budget is consumed, so there is no multiple-comparison exposure to declare.

deliberate_change_from_phase_B.reason: Phase C targets the peak bias. Training on P1 targets whose peaks are 1.6-8.9% systematically low would teach the model a biased peak and defeat the purpose. The P1->P2 shift contributes about 4.3% to peak magnitude, against a measured bias of -27%, so it does not make the attribution ambiguous.
deliberate_change_from_phase_B.baseline_handling: The Phase B treatment checkpoint is re-evaluated against P2 ground truth so the evaluation side is like-for-like.

confirmation_campaign.freshness: geometry ids, mesh ids, mesh-qualified node ids and RNG seeds must be disjoint from every training set and every prior campaign

reported_measures: pooled relative L2 on P, per family, split in-envelope and out-of-envelope
median and distribution of SIGNED relative peak error, with the under/over-prediction split
declared training envelope in derived-ratio space
mean seconds per FEM solve and per operator inference

gates.C.solves: all attempted FEM cases converge, or failures recorded with reasons
gates.C.freshness: campaign disjoint from training and all prior campaigns, asserted
gates.C.envelope: every evaluation case labelled in- or out-of-envelope
gates.C.no-tuning: zero optimizer steps and zero backward calls during the campaign
gates.C.stress: REPORT ONLY - no pass/fail threshold on the stress numbers
gates.C.peak-signed: REPORT ONLY - signed error and under/over split

verdict_policy: This run renders no GO/NO-GO verdict. STEPS-v1.0.md S1 reserves that decision to the human and gives one rule, on the point estimate: <=5% GO, 5-15% GO with contingency, >15% STOP.
